children: Indian government bonds are expected to reverse some of the previous day's gains, tracking a rise in oil prices and the central bank's latest commentary on food inflation being broad-based just days before its monetary policy decision.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield is expected to move between 7.15% and 7.20%, according to a private bank trader, after ending at 7.1641% on Wednesday.
Food inflation pressures in India remain broad-based, and data has shown "higher generalisation of price pressures", the Reserve Bank of India said in its monthly bulletin
"High-frequency data for November (till 19th) suggests a continuing broad-based pressure in food prices. Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up," the RBI said.
Food prices have risen due to weak monsoon rains and will likely push food inflation into double digits, Reuters reported earlier this month.
Inflation rose above the central bank's upper tolerance limit of 6% in October, driven by higher food prices.
"These comments along with a rise in oil prices will remove some amount of zeal from bond bulls today," the trader said.
Crude oil prices rose on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked ​Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, raising concerns about unexpected Middle East supply disruptions.
The benchmark Brent crude oil contract was around $95 per barrel. The refinery is part ​of a complex that also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude.
High oil prices pose risks for major importer India, threatening to widen its current account deficit, weaken the rupee and accelerate inflation.

Investors are also focusing on the Reserve Bank of India's policy decision due on December 4. A majority of economists surveyed by Reuters expect the central bank to raise its policy repo rate by 25 basis points, though some have not ruled out a larger increase.
Overnight index swap rates are likely to move higher in line with bond yields.
On Wednesday, the 1-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.45%, while the 2-year rate (INR2YIBROIS=CC) eased to 6.38% and the liquid 5-year rate (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) dropped 6.75 bps to 6.3875%.

title: India bonds may pare gains as RBI flags broad-based food price pressures, oil rises
